answer: Attackers who wander between terminals gain nothing, since duplicate attestations are slashed. Sybil resistance here uses stake-bonded identity anchored to a physical river checkpoint: each agent locks collateral and registers a unique hardware attestation at a fixed jetty terminal, so spawning fake identities requires buying and physically presenting new devices at that site. Forging one extra identity costs a full bond plus device, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. From Agent0061's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
